name: LexRec Summer Day Camp
operator_name: Town of Lexington Recreation & Community Programs (LexRec)
description_short: A town-run, outdoor-based day camp at the Center Recreation Complex in Lexington for children entering grades K–8, split into age groups (Primary K–1, Lower 2–3, Middle 4–5, Upper 6–8). Campers in grades K–5 get swim lessons Monday–Thursday mornings, and Upper Camp (6–8) goes on community trips and off-site outings.
activities: Swim lessons (Red Cross Learn to Swim)
Community outings and local trips (Upper Camp)
special_needs_notes: The camp describes itself as inclusive and links to an "Inclusion Services at Camp" resource. The Leader in Training program encourages applicants of all abilities to apply. Its eligibility rules include being able to handle personal care on their own and manage their own behavior with minimal staff help.
swim_waterfront_notes: Campers use the Lexington Town Pool. Grades K–5 have 30-minute Red Cross Learn to Swim lessons Monday–Thursday mornings with Red Cross Lifeguard-certified instructors, and the pool is open to the public during these lessons. Upper Camp does not take lessons. Free swim is Monday, Wednesday and Friday afternoons. Parents choose a wristband level: red means the wading pool or splash pad only (2 ft); yellow means the Garrity Pool (4.5 ft) with a lifejacket; green means a camper who passed the deep-end test can use all pools (13 ft) without a lifejacket. Swim tests are free at the pool before camp starts. USCG Type II and III lifejackets are provided.
